name: Cyber-Physical & Autonomous Vehicle Security
description: Security of cyber-physical systems, ICS/SCADA, robotics, drones, and autonomous/connected vehicles.
narrative:
The earliest USENIX Security work in this area focused on the physical trustworthiness of the sensors that cyber-physical systems depend on. "Injected and Delivered: Fabricating Implicit Control over Actuation Systems by Spoofing Inertial Sensors" (2018) showed that an attacker could acoustically spoof inertial sensors to seize implicit control of actuation systems like drones, establishing the recurring theme that physical-layer sensor manipulation, not just software bugs, is the soft underbelly of CPS. Around the same time the field began mapping the attack surface of real vehicles, with "CANvas: Fast and Inexpensive Automotive Network Mapping" (2019) reverse-engineering the in-vehicle CAN network, and supply-chain integrity work like "in-toto: Providing farm-to-table guarantees for bits and bytes" (2019) protecting the software that lands on these devices.

The 2020-2022 period marked a decisive shift toward attacking the machine-learning perception stack of autonomous vehicles. "Towards Robust LiDAR-based Perception in Autonomous Driving" (2020) demonstrated general black-box adversarial sensor attacks against LiDAR and became the area's most-cited paper, while "SAVIOR: Securing Autonomous Vehicles with Robust Physical Invariants" (2020) pushed the defensive counterpart of using physical models to catch sensor tampering. Researchers then broadened the perception attack catalog to lane detection ("Too Good to Be Safe", 2021) and traffic-light recognition ("Rolling Colors: Adversarial Laser Exploits against Traffic Light Recognition", 2022). In parallel, the in-vehicle network and ICS communities matured: "Exposing New Vulnerabilities of Error Handling Mechanism in CAN" (2021) and "CANARY" (2021) deepened CAN attack-and-defense, and "ICSFuzz" (2021) brought instrumented fuzzing to industrial control applications.

By 2023-2025 the area both consolidated and diversified. Defenses grew more principled and systematic, from runtime integrity work like "ARI: Attestation of Real-time Mission Execution Integrity" (2023) and "Opportunistic Data Flow Integrity for Real-time Cyber-physical Systems" (2024) to systematization efforts such as "SoK: Security of Programmable Logic Controllers" (2024). Attacks moved up the autonomy pipeline, from object detection to "A First Physical-World Trajectory Prediction Attack via LiDAR-induced Deceptions" (2024) and to the emerging connected-vehicle setting in "From Threat to Trust: Exploiting Attention Mechanisms for Attacks and Defenses in Cooperative Perception" (2025).

The most recent work signals where the field stands now: physical-world robustness and stealth ("AE-Morpher", 2024; "Invisible but Detected: Physical Adversarial Shadow Attack and Defense on LiDAR Object Detection", 2025), wide-area localization threats like "GNSS-WASP: GNSS Wide Area SPoofing" (2025), and a renewed push on the industrial and IoT side with explainable intrusion detection ("GeCos Replacing Experts", 2025) and "Cyber-Physical Deception Through Coordinated IoT Honeypots" (2025). The trajectory runs from spoofing individual sensors, through breaking ML perception, to defending whole autonomous and industrial systems against physically grounded, increasingly sophisticated adversaries.

milestones.title: Injected and Delivered: Fabricating Implicit Control over Actuation Systems by Spoofing Inertial Sensors
milestones.note: established physical-layer sensor spoofing as a foundational threat to CPS actuation

milestones.title: CANvas: Fast and Inexpensive Automotive Network Mapping
milestones.note: opened up systematic reverse-engineering of the in-vehicle CAN attack surface

milestones.title: Towards Robust LiDAR-based Perception in Autonomous Driving: General Black-box Adversarial Sensor Attack and Countermeasures
milestones.note: the most-cited paper, pivoting the field toward attacking the ML perception stack of AVs

milestones.title: SAVIOR: Securing Autonomous Vehicles with Robust Physical Invariants
milestones.note: popularized physics-based invariant monitoring as a principled AV defense

milestones.title: Rolling Colors: Adversarial Laser Exploits against Traffic Light Recognition
milestones.note: extended adversarial perception attacks to traffic-light recognition with practical laser exploits

milestones.title: SoK: Security of Programmable Logic Controllers
milestones.note: systematized a decade of ICS/PLC security knowledge, marking the field's maturation

milestones.title: From Threat to Trust: Exploiting Attention Mechanisms for Attacks and Defenses in Cooperative Perception
milestones.note: pushed the frontier into connected-vehicle cooperative perception attacks and defenses

milestones.title: GNSS-WASP: GNSS Wide Area SPoofing
milestones.note: demonstrated wide-area localization spoofing, a current threat to vehicle positioning
